headline: Rain chances have jumped for Saturday night, with Charlotte and areas along and east of I-77 now likely to get a beneficial half inch or more, followed by a very warm Monday and then much cooler weather and an uncertain storm chance heading into Thanksgiving.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Friday afternoon stays dry under high pressure, with mid- and high-level clouds slowly increasing and thickening through tonight. Northeast winds around 10 to 12 mph continue east of the mountains, with gusts near 20 to 25 mph becoming possible late tonight around Charlotte and the Piedmont. No watches, warnings or advisories are in effect.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday's highs return to near normal under thickening clouds as rain chances spread in from the south during the day, holding off until later in the afternoon around Charlotte. Saturday night is now the wettest period: rain is likely across the eastern half of the area and nearly certain along and east of I-77, including Charlotte, where half an inch or more is becoming more likely; most other areas should get about a tenth to a third of an inch. Rain tapers off Sunday morning and it turns a bit milder, though cool, damp air trapped against the mountains may hang on for part of the day along with low clouds. Monday looks quite warm, more than 10 degrees above normal as skies clear, with only a few light showers possible in the mountains Monday afternoon and evening; overnight lows stay at least 5 degrees above normal through early next week.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A mostly dry cold front crosses Monday night into early Tuesday, bringing much cooler air, with temperatures near to below normal from Tuesday through the end of the week. Forecasters have low confidence from Wednesday on because the computer models disagree on the details of a complex, wavy jet stream pattern, though there is a weak signal for a storm that redevelops along the Southeast coast midweek. For now there is a chance of rain from Wednesday through at least the first part of Thanksgiving Day, and depending on timing, the mountains could see a brief period of wintry precipitation when it starts.

watch_for: How much rain reaches Charlotte Saturday night; amounts were raised sharply and half an inch or more is now favored along and east of I-77.
Low clouds and cool, damp conditions possibly lingering into Sunday.
Timing of a possible midweek storm around Thanksgiving, including brief wintry weather in the mountains.
confidence: Confidence is increasing in beneficial weekend rain for the Piedmont and in the warm Monday and cooldown Tuesday, but it is low for precipitation timing and type from Wednesday through Thanksgiving.
